title: Jeremiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 29 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 29.

questions.question: Who did Jeremiah send the letter to from Jerusalem?
options: The residue of the elders, priests, prophets, and all the people carried captive to Babylon
The people who remained in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The residue of the elders, priests, prophets, and all the people carried captive to Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:1 states that Jeremiah sent a letter from Jerusalem to the residue of the elders, priests, prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away captive to Babylon.

questions.question: Which king had departed from Jerusalem along with the queen and princes according to Jeremiah 29?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeconiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:2 mentions that Jeconiah the king, the queen, eunuchs, princes, carpenters, and smiths had departed from Jerusalem.

questions.question: By whose hand was the letter sent to Babylon?
options: Elasah the son of Shaphan and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah
questions.correctAnswer: Elasah the son of Shaphan and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:3 states the letter was sent by Elasah the son of Shaphan and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, whom King Zedekiah sent to Nebuchadnezzar.

questions.question: What did the LORD command the captives to do in Babylon?
options: Build houses and dwell in them, plant gardens and eat their fruit
questions.correctAnswer: Build houses and dwell in them, plant gardens and eat their fruit
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:5 commands the captives to build houses, dwell in them, plant gardens, and eat their fruit while in Babylon.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 29, what were the captives advised to do regarding marriage?
options: Take wives, beget sons and daughters, and give daughters to husbands
questions.correctAnswer: Take wives, beget sons and daughters, and give daughters to husbands
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:6 advises the captives to take wives, beget sons and daughters, and give daughters to husbands so they may increase and not diminish.

questions.question: What were the captives instructed to seek for the city where they were taken?
options: Peace, and pray unto the LORD for it
questions.correctAnswer: Peace, and pray unto the LORD for it
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:7 instructs the captives to seek the peace of the city to which they were carried away and to pray to the LORD for it.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD told the captives to trust the prophets and diviners among them who claimed to speak in His name.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:8 warns the captives not to be deceived by prophets and diviners among them who prophesy falsely in the LORD's name.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 29, the LORD promised to visit the captives and fulfill His good word after seventy years in Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:10 states that after seventy years are accomplished in Babylon, the LORD will visit the captives and perform His good word to cause them to return.

questions.question: What kind of thoughts does the LORD say He has toward the captives?
options: Thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give an expected end
questions.correctAnswer: Thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give an expected end
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:11 explains the LORD's thoughts toward the captives are peace, not evil, to give them an expected end.

questions.question: What will happen when the captives call upon and pray to the LORD according to Jeremiah 29?
options: The LORD will hear and hearken unto them
They will be sent to another land
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will hear and hearken unto them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:12 says that when the captives call upon and pray to the LORD, He will hearken unto them.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promises that if the captives seek Him with all their heart, they will find Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:13 states that if the captives seek the LORD with all their heart, they will find Him.

questions.question: In what order does the LORD instruct the captives regarding their actions in Babylon?
options: Build houses, take wives, seek peace, pray to the LORD
Seek peace, build houses, take wives, pray to the LORD
Take wives, build houses, pray to the LORD, seek peace
Pray to the LORD, build houses, take wives, seek peace
questions.correctAnswer: Build houses, take wives, seek peace, pray to the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:5-7 provides instructions in this order: build houses (v5), take wives (v6), seek peace (v7), and pray to the LORD (v7).

questions.question: Who was the king of Judah that sent Elasah and Gemariah to Nebuchadnezzar according to Jeremiah 29?
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:3 states that Zedekiah king of Judah sent Elasah and Gemariah unto Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 29 says the LORD caused the captives to be carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:4 declares that the LORD caused the captives to be carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

questions.question: What reason does Jeremiah 29 give for seeking the peace of the city where the captives live?
options: For in the peace thereof shall ye have peace
So they can conquer the city
To avoid punishment by Babylonian rulers
To prepare for immediate return to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: For in the peace thereof shall ye have peace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:7 states they should seek peace because in the peace of the city they will have peace themselves.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 29 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 29:12, what will happen when the people call upon the LORD and pray to Him?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will hear them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:12 states that if the people call upon the LORD and pray, He will hearken unto them, demonstrating God's readiness to listen to sincere prayer.

questions.question: What condition does Jeremiah 29:13 give for finding God?
options: Seeking Him with all your heart
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking Him with all your heart
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:13 emphasizes that God will be found when people seek Him with all their heart, indicating wholehearted devotion is necessary.

questions.question: What promise does the LORD make in Jeremiah 29:14 regarding the captivity of His people?
options: He will turn away their captivity and gather them from all nations
He will extend their captivity indefinitely
He will punish them with famine
He will abandon them to their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He will turn away their captivity and gather them from all nations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:14 promises that God will end the captivity, gather His people from all the places they were driven, and bring them back to their original land.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 29:15 view the prophets raised up in Babylon according to the people's claim?
options: The LORD did not send them
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD did not send them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:15 shows that the prophets in Babylon, claimed by people to be raised by the LORD, were actually false and not sent by God.

questions.question: What judgment does the LORD declare in Jeremiah 29:17 against the king on David's throne and the people remaining in Jerusalem?
options: He will send sword, famine, and pestilence upon them
He will bless them with peace and prosperity
He will exile them to Babylon
He will restore them to the land
questions.correctAnswer: He will send sword, famine, and pestilence upon them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:17 declares God's judgment through sword, famine, and pestilence against those who stayed in Jerusalem and the king on David’s throne.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 29:18, what will happen to those who remain in Jerusalem and do not heed God's word?
options: They will be persecuted and scattered among all kingdoms as a curse and reproach
They will be protected and prosper
They will return from captivity early
They will receive visions and dreams
questions.correctAnswer: They will be persecuted and scattered among all kingdoms as a curse and reproach
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:18 states that God will persecute those remaining with sword, famine, pestilence, and scatter them as a curse and reproach among all nations.

questions.question: What reason does Jeremiah 29:19 give for the LORD's judgment on those in Jerusalem?
options: They did not listen to God's words sent by His prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They did not listen to God's words sent by His prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:19 explains that the judgment is because they refused to heed God's words sent by His servants the prophets, despite the prophets rising early and being sent.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 29:20, to whom is the word of the LORD specifically addressed?
options: All of the captivity sent from Jerusalem to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: All of the captivity sent from Jerusalem to Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:20 addresses the word of the LORD to all the captivity whom God sent from Jerusalem to Babylon, indicating a message of hope and instruction for the exiles.

questions.question: What fate does Jeremiah 29:21 say will befall Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah who prophesied lies in God's name?
options: They will be delivered into Nebuchadnezzar's hand and slain before the people's eyes
They will be exalted among the people
They will be forgiven and restored
They will be sent to another city
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into Nebuchadnezzar's hand and slain before the people's eyes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:21 pronounces that these false prophets will be handed over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and killed visibly as judgment for their lies.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 29:22 describe the curse taken up by the captivity of Judah in Babylon against the false prophets?
options: That they be like Zedekiah and Ahab who were roasted in the fire
That they be forgiven for their sins
That they be given another chance
That they be made leaders over the people
questions.correctAnswer: That they be like Zedekiah and Ahab who were roasted in the fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:22 says the captivity will curse these false prophets, wishing them to be like Zedekiah and Ahab who were roasted by the king of Babylon, symbolizing divine judgment.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 29:12-14, what will happen if the exiles call on the LORD, pray, and seek Him wholeheartedly?
options: God will hear them, they will find Him, and He will restore their captivity
They will remain in captivity forever
They will be punished more severely
questions.correctAnswer: God will hear them, they will find Him, and He will restore their captivity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:12-14 connects calling, praying, and seeking God with the promise that He will be found, will hear their prayers, and will turn away captivity by restoring them.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 29:17-18 illustrate the consequence for those who did not go into captivity but remained in Jerusalem?
options: They will suffer sword, famine, pestilence, and be scattered as a curse among nations
They will be protected and blessed by God
They will be healed and prosper
They will receive visions from the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They will suffer sword, famine, pestilence, and be scattered as a curse among nations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:17-18 indicates that those remaining in Jerusalem will face severe judgment involving sword, famine, pestilence, and exile, becoming a curse and reproach among nations.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 29:13 teach us about the attitude required to find God?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:13 teaches that seeking God with all one's heart results in finding Him, highlighting wholehearted devotion as necessary.

questions.question: Jeremiah 29:15 states that the LORD has raised up prophets in Babylon for the people to trust. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:15 indicates the people's claim that the LORD raised prophets in Babylon is false; God did not send those prophets.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 29:32, the LORD promises to bless Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants because he taught rebellion. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:32 declares that Shemaiah and his seed will be punished and not dwell among the people because he taught rebellion against the LORD.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 29.

questions.question: What sin did the false prophets mentioned in Jeremiah 29:23 commit?
options: Committed villany, adultery, and spoke lying words in God's name
questions.correctAnswer: Committed villany, adultery, and spoke lying words in God's name
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:23 states that these false prophets committed villany, adultery with their neighbors' wives, and spoke lying words in the name of the LORD, which He had not commanded.

questions.question: Who is Shemaiah the Nehelamite warned about in this chapter?
options: A false prophet sent by God
A true prophet of the LORD
A rebellious prophet who prophesied lies and caused trust in lies
A king who led Israel astray
questions.correctAnswer: A rebellious prophet who prophesied lies and caused trust in lies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:31 describes Shemaiah as one who prophesied without God's sending and caused the people to trust in lies, leading to his punishment.

questions.question: What punishment does God declare for Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants?
options: They shall be exiled to Egypt
They shall not have a man to dwell among the people and will not see the good God does
They will be blessed with many descendants
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not have a man to dwell among the people and will not see the good God does
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:32 states that Shemaiah and his seed will have no one to dwell among the people and will not behold the good God will do for His people because he taught rebellion against the LORD.

questions.question: What role did God appoint Shemaiah to, according to Jeremiah 29:26?
options: Priest in place of Jehoiada to imprison false prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Priest in place of Jehoiada to imprison false prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:26 explains that God made Shemaiah priest instead of Jehoiada and gave him authority over those who made themselves prophets, to imprison them.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God's promise to restore His people after exile, as found in Jeremiah 29:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezra 1:1-4
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:10 promises a return after seventy years of exile, which echoes Ezra 1:1-4 where Cyrus the king of Persia allows the Israelites to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'villany' in Jeremiah 29:23?
questions.correctAnswer: Moral corruption or wickedness
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term translated 'villany' (רָעָה, ra'ah) in Jeremiah 29:23 conveys moral corruption or wickedness, highlighting the sinful nature of the false prophets' actions.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominent in the structure of God's promises and warnings throughout Jeremiah 29?
options: Chiasm, with parallel statements of judgment and restoration
Parable, with a story about a vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm, with parallel statements of judgment and restoration
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29 uses chiasm, where God's promises of peace and restoration (e.g., verses 10-14) are paralleled and contrasted with warnings of judgment on false prophets and rebellious people (verses 15-32), emphasizing the central message.

questions.question: Why did God say He would punish those who did not listen to His prophets, according to Jeremiah 29:19?
options: Because they did not hearken to God's words sent by prophets
Because they built houses in Babylon
Because they kept the Sabbath day
questions.correctAnswer: Because they did not hearken to God's words sent by prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:19 explains that punishment comes because the people did not listen to the words God sent through His servants the prophets, despite their repeated warnings.

questions.question: What advice did Jeremiah give to the exiles in Babylon concerning their lives there, as found in Jeremiah 29:28?
options: Build houses, dwell in them, and plant gardens to eat their fruit
questions.correctAnswer: Build houses, dwell in them, and plant gardens to eat their fruit
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:28 advises the exiles that their captivity will be long, so they should build houses, live in them, and plant gardens for food, indicating settling in and making life in Babylon stable.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 29:17-18, what will happen to those who remained in Jerusalem and did not go into captivity?
options: They will prosper and be protected
They will face sword, famine, and pestilence and be scattered among nations
They will be taken captive by Egypt
They will receive a special blessing
questions.correctAnswer: They will face sword, famine, and pestilence and be scattered among nations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:17-18 prophesies judgment on those remaining in Jerusalem, describing sword, famine, pestilence, and exile to all kingdoms as punishment for disobedience.

questions.question: What command does Jeremiah give regarding how the exiles should seek God, according to Jeremiah 29:13?
options: Seek God with all your heart
questions.correctAnswer: Seek God with all your heart
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:13 instructs the people to seek the LORD wholeheartedly to find Him, emphasizing sincere, full devotion.

questions.question: What is the purpose of seeking the peace of the city where the exiles dwell, as stated in Jeremiah 29:7?
options: So they can escape captivity quickly
For in its peace they will have peace
questions.correctAnswer: For in its peace they will have peace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:7 commands seeking the peace of the city where the exiles live because their own peace depends on the city's peace, showing God's concern for their well-being even in captivity.

questions.question: Which king is mentioned in Jeremiah 29:21 as the one who will punish false prophets like Ahab and Zedekiah?
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:21 states that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon will execute judgment on the false prophets Ahab and Zedekiah.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 29:11 assures the exiles that God's thoughts toward them are of evil and destruction.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:11 clearly states God's thoughts are of peace and not of evil, to give an expected end, contradicting the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 29:12 promises that if the people call upon God and pray, He will listen to them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:12 promises that when the people call and pray to God, He will hear them, assuring a responsive relationship to sincere prayer.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 29 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the Lord instruct the captives in Babylon to do in Jeremiah 29?
questions.correctAnswer: Build houses and plant gardens
questions.explanation: The Lord instructs the captives to build houses and plant gardens in Jeremiah 29:5, indicating they should settle in Babylon rather than expect a quick return to Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 29:11, what are God's thoughts towards His people?
questions.correctAnswer: Thoughts of peace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:11 reveals that God's thoughts toward His people are thoughts of peace and not of evil, promising them an expected end.

questions.question: What will happen after seventy years of captivity, according to Jeremiah 29:10?
options: They will remain in Babylon forever
questions.correctAnswer: They will return to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:10 states that after seventy years, the Lord will visit His people and perform His good word by causing them to return to Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 29:7, what are the captives instructed to seek for the city they are in?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:7 instructs the captives to seek the peace of the city where they are held captive, indicating the importance of their welfare in Babylon.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 29:8 warn the captives against?
questions.correctAnswer: Hearing false prophecies
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 29:8, the Lord warns the captives not to be deceived by their prophets and diviners, who prophesy falsely in His name.

questions.question: What will God do for those who seek Him with all their heart, according to Jeremiah 29:13?
options: He will be found by them
questions.correctAnswer: He will be found by them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:13 states that those who seek the Lord and search for Him with all their heart will find Him, emphasizing the promise of God's availability.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 29:14, what will God do regarding their captivity?
questions.correctAnswer: He will turn it away
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:14 declares that God will turn away their captivity and gather them from all the nations where He had driven them.

questions.question: What instruction is given regarding the false prophets in Jeremiah 29:21?
options: They will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar
They will lead the people back to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:21 states that the false prophets Ahab and Zedekiah will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, indicating God's judgment on them.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 29:19 say about the people in captivity and the false prophets?
options: They listened to God's true prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They ignored God's words
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:19 explains that the captives did not hearken to God's words, which were sent by His prophets, resulting in their judgment.

questions.question: What is the nature of the punishment promised to Shemaiah the Nehelamite in Jeremiah 29:32?
options: He will be punished and have no descendants
questions.correctAnswer: He will be punished and have no descendants
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:32 states that Shemaiah will be punished and will not have a man to dwell among the people, signifying a severe consequence for his false prophecies.

questions.question: What aspect of God is highlighted in Jeremiah 29:11 regarding His plans for the captives?
questions.correctAnswer: His mercy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:11 highlights God's mercy by expressing His intentions of peace and hope for the captives, demonstrating His care for their future.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 29:15 imply about the people's belief in prophets in Babylon?
options: They believed all prophets were false
They thought the Lord had raised up true prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They thought the Lord had raised up true prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:15 indicates that the people believed the Lord had raised up prophets in Babylon, reflecting their desire for divine guidance despite the presence of falsehood.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be derived from the combined teaching of Jeremiah 29:5-6 and Jeremiah 29:11?
options: God desires destruction for His people
God's plan includes their flourishing and future hope
God is indifferent to their suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God's plan includes their flourishing and future hope
questions.explanation: The combined teaching of Jeremiah 29:5-6 and Jeremiah 29:11 reveals that God's plan for His people includes their flourishing in captivity and a hopeful future, demonstrating His faithfulness.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 29:8-9 and Jeremiah 29:19 synthesize to affirm God's sovereignty over false prophecies?
options: God allows false prophets to prosper
False prophets will lead many to truth
questions.correctAnswer: God actively judges false prophecies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:8-9 warns against false prophecies, while Jeremiah 29:19 emphasizes God's judgment on those who did not heed His words, affirming His sovereignty over falsehood.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God is indifferent to human suffering. What does Jeremiah 29:10-11 actually teach?
options: God has no plans for His people
God's plans are for their peace and future hope
questions.correctAnswer: God's plans are for their peace and future hope
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:10-11 teaches that despite their suffering, God has plans for the captives that include peace and a hopeful future, demonstrating His active concern for their well-being.
